newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower after LME stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower after LME stocks rise.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower for a second day, in line with LME copper prices, after a sharp jump in LME warehouse copper stocks.
LME copper stocks rose 17,025 tonnes to 160,325 tonnes.

"The downtrend of the past three weeks continues, as demand eases during the traditionally slow summer period, while stocks are rising, but the market did take some heart from the rise in U.S. industrial output in June," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
U.S. industrial production in June rose 0.3 percent, up from a 0.2 percent rise in May, with automobile output rebounding and the aircraft and hi-tech sectors reported to be strong.
COMEX September copper ended down 0.90 cent at 103.80 cents a pound, with the September/December spread steady at 2.00 cents a pound. Total estimated COMEX copper volume was 9,500 lots.
But the LME cash-to-three month spread fell back to around $188.00 a tonne, after news of the warehouse stocks rise.
COMEX copper prices have tumbled from 12 month highs around 120 cents a pound to a low of 101.50 cents last week, as funds liquidated long positions build during the winter and spring.
